subject: POC access & evaluation plan — Nimbus Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@nimbushealth.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: POC access & evaluation plan — Nimbus Health

Hi Alex / Samira —

Thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned heading into the POC: 

High-level objective:
- Validate Redwood inference runtime against Nimbus Health's production-like workload to assess latency, cost-per-token, and end-to-end reliability for a customer-facing summarization feature.

Success criteria (what success looks like to Nimbus):
- 95th percentile inference latency <= 220ms for 1k token context on the selected model
- Sustained throughput of ~40 req/s with <10% tail latency increase under realistic batching
- Accuracy: ROUGE-L / human spot-checks show parity with current baseline (samples attached in the eval plan)
- No PII exfil incident; logs/auditability retained per your compliance needs

Proposed timeline (3-week POC):
- Week 0 (this week): access & provisioning (SSO invites + IP allowlist + temporary API key), kick-off meeting
- Week 1: run smoke tests and perf baseline on your sample dataset
- Week 2: scale tests and cost analysis; iterate on batching/quantization settings
- Week 3: results review, recommendations, decision checkpoint

Ownership:
- Nimbus: Alex (technical lead), Samira (PM) — will provide evaluation users, sample dataset, and IP ranges to allowlist
- Redwood: Marissa (eng sponsor / sales), Dev (eng lead) — will provision access, create API key, and support test runs

Immediate asks for provisioning (please confirm items below so we can start today):
1) List of evaluator emails to invite to SSO (Okta)
2) Static IPs or CIDR ranges to allowlist on our side
3) Confirm we can share a temporary, scoped API key for the POC (will be rotated after the POC)

Attached: poc-eval-plan.xlsx (evaluation matrix + sample prompts)

If that looks right I’ll: 1) send the SSO invites, 2) create the temp API key and share via secure link, and 3) add your IPs to the allowlist. Also propose a 30-minute kickoff on Thursday to walk through the eval plan.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

--

Hi Alex / Samira —

I’ll take the provisioning work on the Redwood side. Plan below and what I’ll do today: 

1) SSO invites: We use Okta for enterprise SSO invitations. Please confirm the evaluator emails and whether Nimbus requires SCIM provisioning or just an invite link. If just invites, we’ll send them this afternoon.

2) IP allowlist: I’ll add 18.205.36.0/24 and 3.235.80.0/24 to our staging allowlist. Can you confirm if you have any additional CIDRs?

3) Temp API key: I will create a scoped API key named redwood-poc-nimbus-202704 (scope: inference.read, expiry: 30 days). I will NOT include the key inline in email. Instead I will upload a single-use file to our secure transfer link and share the link with an expiration. (Attachment stub below will represent the file we upload.)

4) Test accounts & quotas: I will set the tenant quotas to allow up to 50 req/s and 1M tokens total for the POC. If you need higher limits for a specific test window, let me know the time and we can temporarily bump.

Attachments: redwood-temp-api-key.txt (placeholder - real key will be shared via secure link)

Next steps I will complete today: send SSO invites, add IPs to allowlist, create API key and upload to secure link, and share the link with the three evaluator addresses. I’ll follow up here when each step is done and include the kickoff calendar invite for Thu 4/8 10am PT.

—Dev
